subject: Next steps: ACME trial acceptance plan, timeline, and escalation path
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acmecloud.com>, Priya Sharma <psharma@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps — ACME trial: acceptance criteria, owners, timeline

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have a single source of truth going into the trial.

High-level goal:
- Validate Redwood can meet ACME’s latency SLA for API-driven embeddings and chat generation under your expected mixed workload (30k tokens/day, 1k concurrent requests peak).

Proposed acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
1) 95th percentile latency <= 120ms for chat endpoint during synthetic peak load (as defined in eval plan).
2) End-to-end embedding generation for 10k records completes within nightly window (<= 2 hours).
3) No PII leakage in logs; all request payloads encrypted and access-audited.
4) Integration with your S3 ingestion pipeline (read-only) and ability to attach KV cache with consistent results across sessions.

Timeline:
- Week 0 (next week): provisioning + network whitelisting
- Week 1: baseline perf tests + integration
- Week 2: stress tests & regression checks
- Week 3: final acceptance run and results review

Owners:
- Redwood: Vanessa (trial PM), Marcus (SE - tech lead), Rishi (prod engineer - escalation)
- ACME: Jordan (product), Priya (IT/procurement)

Open items / risks:
- Network egress requirements and firewall rules — ACME IT to confirm
- SOC2 evidence and audit logs — ACME asked for documentation
- Potential blocking bug: long-tail KV cache warm-up causing latency spikes under cold-starts (Marcus to prepare mitigation)

Attachments: rdw-poc-eval-plan-v1.xlsx (evaluation plan), network-requirements.pdf

Next steps / asks:
- Jordan/Priya: confirm you can start provisioning Wednesday 18 Nov and share firewall IPs for whitelisting
- Marcus: share short mitigation plan for KV cache behaviour by EOD Tue
- I’ll create a shared doc for daily status updates and a Jira board for issues.

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — ACME trial: acceptance criteria, owners, timeline

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap.

A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- The 95th percentile latency target is OK but we need the raw latency distribution exported after each test (CSV) so our infra team can validate. Can you include that in the eval outputs?
- For SOC2 evidence: our security team needs an extract of audit logs showing request IDs and access timestamps. Do you have a canned report for that or will that be ad-hoc?

About the schedule: Wed 18 Nov provisioning is fine. I’ll have Gavin from our network team send the firewall IPs by Monday.

Also, Priya called out a compliance item: can you confirm whether request bodies are stored at rest for any duration in your hosted offering? We’ll need explicit confirmation.

Jordan

Jordan —

Quick technical notes and mitigations for the KV cache cold-start long tail:

Summary of issue (repro steps):
- Under cold-start conditions, the first few sessions populate the KV cache and cause 99th percentile latency spikes due to synchronous cache population on the critical path.

Immediate mitigations (for trial):
- Pre-warm cache with representative prefixes (we can run a scripted pre-warm step during provisioning).
- Enable async population for non-critical tokens during initial warm-up window (config toggle).
- Limit initial concurrency during baseline runs to avoid compounding warm-up.

If the above is insufficient we will:
- Roll a temporary kernel-level patch to decouple cache IO (Marcus + Rishi) — target turnaround: 48 hours
- Escalation path: Rishi -> eng on-call -> infra lead (pager)

Deliverables by Tue EOD (17 Nov): short mitigation plan (attached) and pre-warm script in our GitHub repo: https://github.com/redwood/se-scripts/poc-prewarm

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks — we want to tweak acceptance #2: instead of nightly window <=2 hours, can we do a target of <=90 minutes for the initial load? Our data processing SLA is tighter.

Also confirmed: our procurement team will need a short statement that Redwood does not persist request bodies beyond 7 days for the hosted trial (we’ll treat that as a contractual point). Can you provide that in writing?

Proposed trial window: 18 Nov -> 8 Dec (3 weeks). Does that align with Redwood’s availability?

Priya
